prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1071; do not mention it.)
text:
This office represents the injured party in connection with the motor vehicle collision described above. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person. If your insured or any representative of your company has already been in contact with our client, please let us know so that we can address it.

Our client sustained injuries in a low-speed head-on collision and is currently undergoing medical evaluation and treatment. Their full extent of injury and related losses are still being documented, and we will provide a formal demand once that process is complete.

To allow us to evaluate this claim properly, please provide a complete copy of the policy declarations page and disclose the bodily injury and property damage liability limits applicable to your insured for this loss. Please also confirm in writing whether any excess or umbrella coverage may apply.

We further request that your company preserve all evidence relating to this incident. This includes photographs, vehicle inspection and repair records, event data recorder or telematics information, recorded statements, claim file notes, adjuster reports, and all communications with your insured or any third party. Please ensure that no such materials are altered, discarded, or repaired without prior notice to this office.
